newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 22.51 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 22.51 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs VE6MTMA=RR fell 135 basis points to 22.51 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 30 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 23.86 percent coupon for a price of 100.60 percent. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 23.86 percent

The bank also sold ten billion bolivars of 269-day notes VE9MTMA=RR with a 24.57 percent coupon at a price of 100.13 percent, and ten billion bolivars of 358-day notes VE1YTMA=RR with a 25.29 percent coupon at an average price of 99.99 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 105 basis points to 24.37 percent for the 269-day bills, and 122 basis points to 25.30 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
